vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.6.6

The 'agent-chronicle' skill is a professional and well-documented tool designed to allow AI agents to maintain a reflective diary. The code logic is clearly aligned with its stated purpose, gathering context from local session logs to generate journal entries via OpenClaw-native sub-agent spawning (sessions_spawn). The scripts (generate.py, setup.py, export.py) use secure coding practices, such as the --sandbox flag for pandoc and list-based subprocess calls to prevent command injection. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized network calls, or malicious prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are consistent with its stated purpose (agent-perspective diary generation); it asks for no credentials and uses only local files and optional local/external rendering tools, but it does read the agent's session/memory files and can spawn sub-agents so you should review privacy/auto-generation settings before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI diary) align with the included scripts and SKILL.md: the code collects session logs and persistent diary files, builds a generation task for a sub-agent, saves entries to memory/diary/, and exports via pandoc/WeasyPrint. Required binaries list only python3 which is appropriate for the provided Python scripts. Minor inconsistency: README and scripts expect pandoc / weasyprint / markdown libraries for exports but the declared required binaries list only python3.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and generate.py explicitly instruct the agent to gather recent session logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md), persistent diary files (quotes.md, curiosity.md, etc.), and emit a task for a sub-agent via sessions_spawn. This is expected for a diary generator, but it means the skill reads potentially sensitive conversation history and writes summaries back into memory. Also, export HTML uses a remote CSS URL (cdn.simplecss.org), which will cause an outbound fetch during export.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only install) and all code files are shipped in the skill bundle. Nothing in the manifest downloads or executes remote installers. Optional dependencies (pandoc, texlive, weasyprint, Python markdown) must be installed by the user; that requirement is documented in README/scripts but not declared in the top-level requirements metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials and no config paths in the manifest. At runtime the scripts look for OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE (and common workspace locations) to find the memory folder — this is proportional to the task. No extraneous secrets or unrelated service tokens are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not 'always' enabled and uses normal agent capabilities (it expects to spawn OpenClaw sub-agents via sessions_spawn). Autonomous invocation of sub-agents is part of the platform model and not, by itself, a red flag. The skill writes files into the agent workspace under memory/diary/ (its own storage) and does not modify other skills' configurations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: gather recent session logs and diary files and produce first-person diary entries via a spawned sub-agent. Before installing, consider: 1) privacy: it reads your agent's memory/session logs (may include sensitive user data). If you are uncomfortable storing or exporting that content, disable memory integration, set privacy_level to 'private', or point diary_path to a location you control. 2) exports: PDF/HTML export can call pandoc/WeasyPrint and (for HTML) fetch a remote CSS file — that causes outbound network requests. 3) dependencies: install pandoc/weasyprint/markdown only if you need export features; python3 alone runs generation/setup. 4) automation: auto_generate can create entries automatically — turn it off if you prefer manual control. No API keys or other credentials are requested by the skill. If you want extra assurance, review config.json and the scripts (generate.py, setup.py, export*.py) in your environment before enabling auto-generation or sharing exported files.
